gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named measurement for any CD radio. The closest one available is Archimago's bench test of a Sony CFD-S05 boombox's CD playback. He measured an effective dynamic range of about 12 bits, against the CD format's 16. The cause was a high noise floor, audible with the volume turned up a little.
standout_why: I opened three rival pages. dailydealhere.com/best-cd-boomboxes gives only maker specs (wattage, presets, weight) and says it does no lab testing. bestspeakerreviews.com/best-cd-am-fm-stereo-system gives maker specs only (for example, the Panasonic SC-PM270 at 20 W RMS) and no measured figures. The loudersound.com article body would not load, and it is a hi-fi CD player list, not a list of CD radios. The other results are Sony spec pages, manuals and retailer listings. None of them has a measurement, so anything I found is new. But the only real measurement is of an older Sony boombox that is not one of the candidates. The only named outside verdict on a candidate is a grade, not a figure. So the finding barely adds to the answer.
decides: It doesn't decide the pick. Over about 15 searches I found no RTINGS, Notebookcheck, SoundGuys, What Hi-Fi?, Fnac Labo, Stiftung Warentest or ASR measurements for the GPX BC112B, Jensen CD-490, CD-560 or JCR-310, Sony CFD-S70, Philips TAZ6000 or Panasonic SC-PM270. The page should compare candidates on maker specs and price, not on measurements. Two weak pointers back that up. The CFD-S05 test suggests cheap Sony boomboxes have a high CD noise floor. audiovision rated the Philips TAZ6000 'ausreichend' (sufficient) and called its sound quality 'bescheiden' (modest), which is a mark against the Philips card ChatGPT showed. Neither finding singles out one model.

findings.product: Sony CFD-S05 (older Sony CD/cassette/radio boombox; not a current candidate)
findings.label: Effective dynamic range, CD playback (headphone output)
findings.source_title: Archimago's Musings: MEASUREMENTS: What Lo-Fi Looks Like (Sony CFD-S05)
findings.note: Measured by Archimago. Posted 25 Feb 2013; first posted on the Squeezebox Forum 13 Feb 2013. Setup: a test CD-R played through the boombox's headphone jack with MegaBass off, recorded on an E-MU 0404USB. He blames a high noise floor, audible with the volume up a little. He also called the THD and frequency response poor, but gave them only as graphs, with no numbers.

findings.note: Test by audiovision magazine, issue 10/2025, published 19 Sep 2025. I read it secondhand through the testberichte.de aggregator, not in audiovision itself. No sub-scores or measured figures were given. The TAZ6000 is the EU DAB+/FM model. The 'Philips Portable CD Player with Bluetooth, FM Radio, USB' card ChatGPT showed at Walmart may be a different US model.

unsourced: Measured loudness (dB SPL), battery runtime or frequency response for the Jensen CD-490, CD-560 or JCR-310 and the GPX BC112B. Searched RTINGS, ASR, Archimago and general 'tested/measured' reviews; I found only maker specs and unnamed affiliate roundups.

Bench measurements of the Sony CFD-S70. Searched English, German and French sources, Archimago and ASR; I found only Sony specs and user reviews. The bestradios.co.uk review that came up in search was not opened and was not shown to include measurements.

Lab measurements of the Panasonic SC-PM270 or SC-PM272. Searched Les Numériques, Fnac L'Éclaireur Test Labo (it has tested only the SC-PMX80, PMX150, PMX802 and SA-PMX92) and Stiftung Warentest; none covered the SC-PM270 or PM272.

Measured runtimes for the CD boomboxes. An Alibaba-hosted buying guide claims it measured runtimes (for example, a Jensen CD-785 at 5.7 hours) but names no tester. I left it out under the named-source rule.
